findings.title: A receipt written after the unverified thing is swallowed as part of it: 18 of 20 claims that name the attempt and how it failed in their own sentence are blocked, including the README's own receipt forms 'from the docs', 'per the README' and '50 runs'.
findings.rule_quoted: 'couldn't verify', 'unable to confirm', 'not available', 'no data exists' and their variants ... may be written only when the same sentence names what was attempted and how it failed.  ||  a receipt | in the claim's own sentence and outside the words that say what was not verified: an attempt (ran, tried, searched, ... "the re-run", "50 runs", "from the docs", "per the README", "using X"), a failure mode (returned, timed out, denied, refused, failed, error, a 4xx or 5xx code, ...)
findings.rule_source: fixed/hooks/README.md:502-505 and README.md:535; decisions.md:41-42 ('A fix that closes a bypass by blocking ordinary use is rejected')

Independent list FR (receipts phrased freely): == FR: 15/20 ... mismatches: FR01 FR02 FR07 FR17 FR20 (e.g. 'Data for last week is not available: the export query returned zero rows.' blocked). The merged gate on the same RE list: 13/23.
findings.expected: allow: each sentence names the attempt (ss, the health endpoint, 50 runs, the changelog, the README, the curl) and how it failed (permission denied, 503, refused, timed out) in the claim's own sentence, which is what the rule asks for and what the README lists as receipts.
findings.how_it_arises: Ordinary. The receipt is read only outside 'the words that say what was not verified', and that span runs to the next colon, semicolon, bracket or one of a list of clause words. A comma followed by 'the', 'a', 'which' or a number, and any preposition ('in 50 runs', 'from the changelog', 'per the README'), do not end it, so the receipt is counted as part of the unverified thing. This is the most natural way to write a receipt ('X, which returned Y'; 'X, the API returned 500'), so the honest behaviour the gate exists to produce is blocked. One block per stretch, then silent. Row shapes: owner row + one assistant text row, as selftest_rows builds them (real shapes).

findings.title: An ordinary working note between tool calls ('I couldn't find the config where I expected it. Let me search the whole repository.') blocks the stop even when the next tool call settles it and the final answer is clean: 10 of 10 such turns blocked, against 2 of 10 on the merged gate.
findings.component: fixed/hooks/receiptlaw.py decide() + turngate.Model.prose (every text of the stretch is judged)
findings.rule_quoted: A false block is a defect too ... A gate that blocks honest work teaches the owner to ignore it. A fix that closes a bypass by blocking ordinary use is rejected.  ||  (brief) The gate blocks a stop whose answer holds such a claim with no receipt, once.  ||  (README) A claim in an earlier text of the stretch counts, also when a later lookup settled it: say so in the sentence ("at first I couldn't ..."), or give the note its receipt.
findings.rule_source: decisions.md:41-42 and decisions.md:39 ('add no new block on honest work'); fixed/hooks/README.md:517-521
findings.observed:

fixed: block N05 note: I wasn't able to confirm the port from the docs. Checking the running process instead.

fixed: == 10 of 10 ordinary turns blocked for a working note the next tool call settled
merged (1ce99d5): == 2 of 10 ordinary turns blocked for a working note the next tool call settled
findings.expected: allow: the note is followed by the attempt itself (a Bash call that finds the value) and the final answer carries its receipt; no inability is left standing in what the stop answers with. At the least, no new block on this honest pattern relative to the merged gate.
findings.how_it_arises: Ordinary agent work: narrating a miss and the next step between tool calls. The README chose to judge every text of the stretch (closing TB-5's report-then-reload shape) and makes the assistant pre-empt the gate with 'at first I couldn't'. The documents disagree on what is judged (the brief and the owner's words: the answer; the README: every text), so this is also an ambiguity the owner should settle. On either reading it is a new block on honest work (8 more of 10 than before). Real row shapes (selftest_rows).

findings.title: A results table whose header holds 'Test', 'Case' or 'Input' is taken for a table of examples, so every bare claim in it passes: 4 of 5 ordinary status tables with 'could not verify' / 'unverified' rows are let through.
findings.rule_quoted: not a claim: ... a row of a table of examples  ||  a claim | ... "X is unverified / unconfirmed / unverifiable" as a predicate, a label or a table cell
findings.observed:
MISMATCH SH01   want=block got=allow | Test | Status | ... | deploy health | could not verify |
ok       SH02   want=block got=block | Check | Result | ... | deploy health | could not verify |
MISMATCH SH03   want=block got=allow | Test | Result | ... | live plugin version | unverified |
MISMATCH SH04   want=block got=allow Results: | Case | Outcome | ... | weekly task | couldn't confirm it ran |
MISMATCH SH05   want=block got=allow | Input file | Status | ... | b.csv | couldn't verify the totals |
ok       SH16   want=allow got=allow | Test | Status | ... | deploy health | pass (curl returned 200) |
findings.expected: block: each table is the assistant's own status report of its own checks, and the cell 'could not verify' / 'unverified' names no attempt. Only a table that lists example sentences or phrases is exempt.
findings.how_it_arises: Ordinary: '| Test | Status |' is the commonest shape of a verification summary at the end of technical work. A header cell holding any of case, example, text, input, expected, verdict, fixture, test (and others) turns the whole table into 'examples'. The README states only 'a row of a table of examples' and does not disclose that a test-status header makes the table exempt. The same table with the header 'Check' blocks (SH02). Real row shapes.

findings.title: An inability stated through the assistant's own work as subject passes: 'This run couldn't confirm the corrections rate.', 'My search couldn't find the config.', 'The weekly review couldn't verify the plugin version.' (10 of 10 let through).
findings.rule_quoted: a claim | the assistant (I, we, "this session", or no subject at all) could not verify, confirm ... something  ||  An inability claim ("couldn't verify" and its variants, contractions included) needs a receipt in the same sentence.

findings.expected: block: 'this run', 'my search', 'the weekly review' are the assistant's own work in its own report. The sentence is the assistant's inability claim with no attempt named, just as 'I couldn't confirm the corrections rate.' (blocked) is.
findings.how_it_arises: Ordinary in unattended reports (a scheduled run writes 'This run couldn't ...'), where nobody is watching and the rule matters most. Any subject other than I/we/this session/container/sandbox/environment/assistant/agent is read as somebody else's. Not among the README's stated limits. Real row shapes.

findings.rule_quoted: Because this gate blocks a stop, it was then read against ordinary prose ...: statements about code, conditions, reported speech and search results that claim no inability are let through, and what is still blocked wrongly is listed as a limit
findings.observed: distinct files read 461 / sentences 44560 / sentences with a standing claim 44 / blocked sentences (distinct) 25. Among them: '| Unconfirmed | 0 |' (a tally cell); 'CANNOT VERIFY closed - he is on no pool row, so correctly absent'; '... UNVERIFIABLE until 2026-10-24, because those box scores don't exist yet.'; 'I didn't find an official box score, so exact minutes for Lillard and Holiday remain unconfirmed.'; '... findings.expected: Either these classes are let through, or the README lists them as known false blocks: a receipt in a comma clause or after a preposition (AR-1), 'don't exist' / 'didn't find' as failure modes, 'unverifiable until <time>' (a time, not an inability), a tally cell, a working note (AR-2).
findings.how_it_arises: The grammar was tuned on the same corpora it was measured on (prose-scan.md section 4 lists each change made from a block found there). On a corpus it never saw, about 4 in 10 of the blocked sentences are false blocks, not 0. The prose is the owner's own projects.

findings.title: After the OTHER Stop gate's block, a retried answer that is text only and missing from the record is never judged, though the Stop input holds it: the block is not counted because no assistant row follows it, and the retry flag then lets the stop go.
findings.component: fixed/hooks/receiptlaw.py decide() lines 'if data.get("stop_hook_active") and not model.feedback(start)' + turngate.Model.feedback (turngate.py:2034)

not_verified: The plugin wrapper's comment (plugin/core-governance/scripts/run-unless-project-wired.sh:16 and plugin/core-governance/README.md:29) says the receipt gate 'keeps per-session sentinels, so they do not double-fire'; the rebuilt gate has no sentinel. By reading, two copies at one stop block together once and are then both silent, so there is no double block across stops; not run against a real two-copy session.

The block reason itself advertises an escape ('put them in quotation marks'): a claim the assistant wraps in quotes is never judged. This follows from the README's own rule; I did not measure how often it would be used.
notes: Regression list: all 9 findings are fixed in their stated cases. The remaining mismatches (Q01/Q02, S05, Y01, T06, E01) are builder defaults or stated limits, none of them an owner decision. The main risk is now the other direction: limiting the receipt to 'the claim's sentence, outside the unverified thing' blocks the honest receipt shapes (AR-1) and working notes (AR-2) far more often than the merged gate did, and the builder's measurement did not include those shapes. Fixtures use the fixed library's own row builders (selftest_rows: shapes observed on a real record). The builder's 174-break list re-run: 174 caught (claim holds); my own breaks found one unpinned rule (AR-7). MORE: three of my 65 ordinary sentences are blocked: 'I was unable to reproduce the flakiness in 50 runs, so ...' (AR-1 class), 'The logs are unavailable for jobs that ran on spot instances, because those instances are deleted.' (a fact about a system with its reason), 'The certificate could not be verified by older Android clients, which lack the new root.' (passive with another agent named by 'by'); bb/out-sentences.txt. MORE: four of five facts about data in the rule's literal words ('No data exists for the 2019 season because the league started in 2020.') are blocked; arguably the rule's words, listed as edge (FBE). MORE: the plugin wrapper comment and the plugin README still say the receipt gate keeps per-session sentinels (drift, low; see not_verified). Report saved as WORK/fa-receipt/findings.json.
